source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue allopurinol and observe at home, because a drug-related rash cannot progress to a serious syndrome.","B":"Apply a topical cream only, because allopurinol-associated rash does not require medication review or clinical assessment.","C":"Stop allopurinol and obtain prompt medical evaluation because serious hypersensitivity skin reactions may occur.","D":"Double the next allopurinol dose, because rash generally indicates inadequate urate lowering rather than drug toxicity."}}
source_row.rationale: A new rash during allopurinol therapy requires prompt action because labeling directs discontinuation at the first rash/sign of hypersensitivity and warns of severe cutaneous reactions including SJS/TEN.
source_row.source_detail: Warnings and precautions: discontinue allopurinol permanently at the first appearance of skin rash or other signs that may indicate hypersensitivity; serious and sometimes fatal reactions including SJS/TEN are described. DailyMed allopurinol label version 103, current in 2026; rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client taking allopurinol develops a new rash. Which action is most appropriate?
